Subject: Exec workshop: Incident protocols & local resources — draft

Hi all,

As we lock in the on-site executive workshop for Acme (Aug 26–28), I put together an initial set of health & safety protocols and local resource routing so we have a clear playbook if anything happens during travel or on-prem. This is a draft — please review and flag gaps by EOD Wednesday. Key goals: short response times for medical incidents, clear escalation chain, and pre-identified vendor options for med-evac/transport.

Draft highlights (attached):
- Primary on-site contact and backup for Redwood and Acme
- Local urgent care / hospital list within 20 miles
- Med-evac vendor recommendation and insurance notes
- Simple incident flow: stabilize -> notify -> escalate to exec + legal -> med-evac if needed
- Travel advisory check cadence (72/24 hours before travel)

Immediate asks:
1) Marcus — can you confirm vendor procurement constraints (insurance min coverage, PO timing)?
2) Monica — please check our emergency contact escalation for attendees (confirm legal/CS rep availability).
3) Stephanie — can you run this by Acme (Sara) and confirm their local site lead and parking/entry requirements?

Attachments: KP_Exec_Workshop_Health_Protocol_v1.pdf (draft)

I looped in Anna at GlobalSafe — Anna, can you provide the local EMS contacts and any region-specific advisories for the city?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Operations | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: KP_Exec_Workshop_Health_Protocol_v1.pdf (pdf)]

Subject: Re: Exec workshop: Incident protocols & local resources — draft

Kimberly — good start. A few procurement notes based on our vendor guidelines: 

- Insurance: vendors must carry at least $5M general liability + $1M professional liability for med-evac services. Confirmed with Finance last quarter.
- PO timing: for external med-evac contracts we need procurement sign-off 14 days before service start; we can add a clause for on-call activation charges.
- Preferred vendors: GlobalSafe (Anna) is approved for emergent transport; we have a pending quote from AirMedix for international coverage.

I attached the vendor-vetting matrix and the insurance-summary PDF for quick reference. I also noted a vendor clause we should add about data handling during incident coordination (we can’t share any medical details beyond name and critical status without explicit consent).

If we need to book a standby ambulance or on-call nurse, we should decide by Aug 12 to meet procurement timelines.

- Marcus
Director, Procurement | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: vendor-vetting-matrix.xlsx (xlsx)]
[Attachment: insurance-summary.pdf (pdf)]

Thanks for the ping, Kimberly — glad to support. Attached is a compact CSV with local EMS and hospital contacts, plus a two-page region advisory. Top-line items:

- Nearest full-service hospital (24/7 ER): St. Vincent General — 12 miles, trauma center on site.
- 3 urgent care locations within 10 miles for minor issues.
- Med-evac partner: AirRapid. Estimated mobilization: 60–90 mins depending on traffic; they meet the $5M GL requirement.
- Local embassy/consulate advisory: register attendees if they are non-US citizens; we can assist with that.

We recommend the following additions to your protocol:
- On-call local nurse (8am–8pm) for the workshop days; if overnight medication monitoring is a concern, escalate to med-evac.
- Pre-travel health check questionnaire for attendees (loss of smell, fever, recent exposures) to be completed 72 hours prior.
- A single incident coordinator phone number (we can provide a staffed line during the event).

Attachments: Local_EMS_contacts.csv; Region_Advisory_Aug2025.pdf

Happy to hop on a 15-min call to walk through logistics.

—Anna
Operations Lead, GlobalSafe Travel
